title.narrative: Pilot to demonstrate the commercial viability of SweepSmart’s smart waste facility in India

description.narrative: India is facing tremendous issues due to its unmanaged waste streams. Waste is being dumped in nature, on huge landfills or burned on the streets which leads to pollution of water and air and poses serious risks for the environment and public health. In big cities like Bangalore a shocking number of people actually live on these landfills and make a living as waste pickers, an undignified life with many physical dangers. Dutch company SweepSmart saw an opportunity to improve this situation using their experience to set-up waste sorting facilities to work with informal waste pickers to sort waste to enable further recycling. To prepare for future investments, upscaling and to demonstrate the viability of smart waste centers in the Indian context, Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA) therefore provided support to set-up 3 pilot locations for professional dry waste facilities in India. The project aimed to test their operational, commercial and financial feasibility in the Indian context and to improve the lives and working conditions of waste pickers by providing European knowledge and technology through collaboration with local cooperatives that organize informal waste pickers. The facilities were set-up in and around Bangalore and the project directly supported 79 jobs, indirectly supported 100 jobs and offered dry waste sorting and recycling training to 75 people. Furthermore, the project created awareness on improved waste practices amongst 150 people and contributed to organising informal waste pickers, mostly women, and considerably improved their livelihoods. Further investments and scale up of the project are currently being explored and 10 new sorting facilities will be set up in the foreseeable future.
